sentences.text: Arambourgia is an extinct genus containing only one species of alligatorine crocodile found in Europe.
This animal possessed non-serrated teeth and a deep snout, distinguishing it from the flatter snouts of most other alligatorids.
The genus Arambourgia was established by Kälin in 1940.
The type species of the genus Arambourgia is Alligator gaudryi, which was originally described by de Stefano in 1905.
Based on its unusual anatomy and karstic fossil settings, Arambourgia gaudryi likely occupied an ecological niche similar to modern juvenile and dwarf crocodilians.
Arambourgia belongs to the family Alligatoridae.
It is classified within the class Reptilia.
The parent group for Arambourgia is the subfamily Alligatorinae.
Recent studies consistently classify Arambourgia within the subfamily Alligatorinae, though its exact placement remains disputed.
Fossils of Arambourgia date to the Late Eocene epoch.
